findings.text: [A]: the numeral 4 is a tiny speck at the bottom; at the smallest tinted size it vanishes, so the icon reads as a generic night landscape, and its home-screen label is truncated to "Paint by Mo...".
[B]: the moon's purple blotches read as craters or stains rather than painted regions, and in the bedtime-dimmed view the dark tile nearly merges with the dark screen, leaving a floating disc.

[C]: the big serif 6 is the boldest numeral in the set and survives every size and the two-tone reduction, so it says 'numbers' best; but in tinted and dimmed views the hills read as a blank card, and the name Paint by Heart says nothing about photos or night.

[D]: crescent plus a 3 sitting inside it is the simplest silhouette and holds up at all three tinted sizes and in two tones, but a dark tile with a white crescent sits squarely among the Sleep sounds rivals (White Noise, Sleep Sounds), so it can read as a sleep app.
[B] and [D] use the short home-screen name 'Moonlight', which fits without truncation but drops 'Paint', so on the home screen only the small numeral signals what the app does.
All four stand apart from the busy, saturated flower-and-heart icons of the paint-by-number category; the calm night palette is distinctive there, though it borrows the sleep category's look.
